q: Is my company eligible for the SBTi SME target route?
title: Who qualifies for the SBTi SME route?
short: Under the SBTi's revised SME definition, you qualify if you are an independent company, not a subsidiary of a larger group, with fewer than 250 employees, turnover under 50 million euros and total assets under 25 million euros, and you are not a financial institution or oil and gas company. Check the current criteria before applying.

ol: Not a subsidiary whose parent group is above these limits. A group decides for its members.
Not a financial institution and not in the oil and gas sector.
Not in a sector where the SBTi requires a sector-specific route, such as companies that must set land-use (FLAG) targets.
p: You must meet every point. Failing one sends you to the standard validation route.

sections.h: What the limits mean in rupees
p: As a rough guide, 50 million euros is about Rs 450 to 500 crore of turnover and 25 million euros about half that in assets, depending on the exchange rate on the date you check. Use your audited figures for the last financial year and the exchange rate the SBTi form asks for.

sections.h: What you commit to on the SME route
ul: A predefined near-term target for Scope 1 and 2, in line with 1.5°C, currently framed as a 42% absolute cut by 2030.
A commitment to measure and reduce Scope 3, without a numeric Scope 3 target.
Annual public reporting of emissions and progress.
A flat fee that is lower than the standard route; check the current fee schedule.

sections.h: What you need before you apply
ul: A Scope 1 and 2 baseline for the base year, built from fuel invoices and electricity bills.
Your boundary choice, normally operational control, applied to every site.
A first view of your largest Scope 3 categories, since you commit to measuring them.

senseible: Senseible builds the Scope 1 and 2 baseline from your fuel invoices and electricity bills, with the factor and source on every line, which is the core data the SME route needs. It does not submit or validate targets; the SBTi does that.
